_comment: Hardware of the Microduck-look build: what drives each joint, the signal map and the supply. Generated by scripts/run_look.py from the reports; the sources are the makers' pages.
licence_line: Microduck-look parts: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, adapted from Pollen Robotics' Microduck; not for commercial use
signal_notes: Baseline: two UNO Q boards, each under one Braccio shield. The shield's six outputs are the UNO Q pins 11, 10, 9, 6, 5 and 3, the only six PWM pins of the header, so one board cannot drive twelve servos through two shields.

The two boards have to act as one controller: one link between them (UART on D0 and D1, 3.3 V, crossed, common ground) or both as targets of one host. The control core in this repository handles six joints on one board; fifteen joints on two boards is not written.

The three small servos are on a 16-channel PCA9685 driver on the first board's I2C (Qwiic connector, 3.3 V logic; the PCA9685 takes 2.3 to 5.5 V logic). Its servo rail is fed with 5 V from the first shield's supply.
Alternative: one UNO Q and one PCA9685 for all fifteen servos, with the shields used only to distribute 5 V. It saves a board and the link, and needs the twelve Braccio leads on the driver's headers.

supply.note: Stall currents of the Braccio servos are assumed (2.0 A and 1.0 A, config/hardware.json); the small servo's 0.75 A is M5Stack's figure.

parts.name: SR431 servo (TinkerKit Braccio kit)
parts.note: hip roll, hip pitch, knee and ankle of each leg; from two kits

parts.name: SR311 servo (TinkerKit Braccio kit)
parts.note: hip yaw of each leg, neck pitch, head pitch; from two kits

parts.name: Arduino UNO Q with a Braccio shield
parts.note: one per leg: six outputs each; on the back plate, one above the other

parts.name: Braccio kit supply, regulated 5 V 4 A
parts.note: one per shield; below the stall demand of six servos: see Power

parts.name: M5Stack Servo Kit 180 (two 9 g position servos per kit)
parts.note: to order: head yaw, head roll and beak need three position servos. The Servo Kit 360 and the BALA-C's servos turn continuously and cannot hold a joint

parts.name: 16-channel I2C servo driver board (PCA9685)
parts.note: to order unless one of your driver boards is this type: the three small servos; on the first UNO Q's Qwiic connector, 3.3 V logic

parts.name: Servo horn with centre screw (from the kits)
parts.note: also the drilling jig for the printed horn plates

parts.name: Horn screws for the printed plates
parts.note: two opposed per horn; size to suit your horns: measure

parts.name: Small cable tie
parts.note: one round each servo cradle in its groove, four for the two board stacks

parts.name: M3 x 10 screw
parts.note: four through the body halves into the frame posts, one through the back of the head; they cut their own thread in the 2.8 mm holes

parts.name: M3 x 16 screw
parts.note: pivots opposite a horn: neck (right upright), head roll (front of the carrier), beak (right cheek)

parts.name: Switch in each servo supply, within reach
parts.note: a software stop does not cut power
